{{Cuisine of Indonesia}}

'''Soto''' (also known as '''sroto''', '''tauto''', '''saoto''', or '''coto''') is a traditional [[Indonesian cuisine#National dishes|Indonesian]] soup mainly composed of broth, meat (such as chicken), and vegetables. Many traditional soups are called ''soto'', whereas foreign- and Western-influenced soups are called ''sop''.

Soto is sometimes considered Indonesia's [[national dish]],<ref name="Kompas.com-Makanan-Nasional">{{Cite news|url=https://travel.kompas.com/read/2018/04/10/171000627/kemenpar-tetapkan-5-makanan-nasional-indonesia-ini-daftarnya|title=Kemenpar Tetapkan 5 Makanan Nasional Indonesia, Ini Daftarnya – Kompas.com|last=Media|first=Kompas Cyber|work=KOMPAS.com|access-date=2018-04-18|language=id}}</ref> as it is served from [[Sumatra]] to [[West Papua (region)|Papua]], in a wide range of variations. Soto is available everywhere from [[warung]]s and open-air eateries to fine-dining restaurants and luxurious hotels.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eatingasia.typepad.com/eatingasia/2009/03/soto-crawl.html| title= A Soto Crawl |work= Eating Asia|date=March 21, 2009 |access-date=July 7, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=October 29, 2011 |title=Indonesia – Soto Ayam at Malioboro Country |url=http://chowhound.chow.com/topics/814793 |access-date=August 15, 2014 |publisher=Chowhound}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Sompotan |first=Johan |date=January 1, 2012 |title=Soto Siap Susul Rendang |url=http://www.okefood.com/read/2011/12/30/299/549520/soto-siap-susul-rendang |access-date=August 15, 2014 |publisher=Okezone.com}}</ref><ref name="Food.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.food.com/recipe/indonesian-chicken-noodle-soup-soto-ayam-187775 | publisher=Food.com | title=Indonesian Chicken Noodle Soup (Soto Ayam)| date=September 26, 2006 |access-date= August 15, 2014}}</ref>

Due to the proximity and significant numbers of Indonesian migrants in neighbouring countries, soto can also be found in [[Singapore]] and [[Malaysia]].

Introduced to [[Suriname]] by [[Javanese Surinamese|Javanese migrants]], it is part of the national cuisine of that country as well, where it is spelled '''saoto'''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.multiculticooking.com/2009/01/03/saoto-soup-surinamese-javanese/|title=Saoto Soup (Surinamese-Javanese) |date=3 January 2009 |publisher =multiculticooking.com |access-date =April 29, 2013}}</ref>
